73818444cf4b1386: CUPERTINO, Sept 10 — Apple unveiled its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, yesterday, kicking off the era of new CEO John Ternus.
The foldable is a crucial test for Apple, which has not launched a breakout hit since the AirPods 10 years ago.
Wednesday’s event was the first under Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1.

Ternus, 51, joined Apple’s product design team in 2001 and worked his way up to leading the engineering teams behind Apple’s entire product lineup, including the iPhones that generate most of the company’s revenue.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Apple’s new iPhone Duo is on display during the ‘Surprise and Shine’ event at the company’s corporate headquarters, Apple Park, on September 9, 2026 in Cupertino, California. The event featured Apple product announcements and was Apple CEO John Ternus’s first keynote address in his new role. — Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images North America/Getty Images pic via AFP

The Duo, roughly shaped like a passport when folded, essentially combines the portability of a smartphone with the larger display of a tablet, offering users a bigger screen without carrying a tablet-sized device.
The product has a full external display when closed, a larger internal display when open, and multiple camera lenses.
The Cupertino-based company said it had reduced the visible crease in the middle of the screen — one of the main criticisms levelled at foldables.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Apple’s new iPhone Duo is on display during the ‘Surprise and Shine’ event at the company’s corporate headquarters, Apple Park in Cupertino, California September 9, 2026. — Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images North America/Getty Images pic via AFP
It is priced starting at US$1,999 (RM8,134), slightly more than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8.
Apple also announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, priced at US$1,199 and US$1,299 respectively, or US$100 more than the iPhone 17 lineup at launch last year.
They will come with an improved camera that allows users to adjust the lens aperture.
Notably, Apple did not announce a cheaper base version of its iPhone, presumably called the iPhone 18, which could indicate it will launch at a later date.

Customers in the United States will be able to pay for new phones, iPads, Macs and Apple Watches in monthly instalments through Apple Upgrade, a leasing programme offered with the buy-now-pay-later giant Klarna.
For the newest lineup of iPhones, a lease through Apple Upgrade works out to around US$50 a month and up.
In late June, the company raised the prices of its Macs and iPads, citing the impact of component shortages caused by the boom in AI, and then warned in July that smartphones would follow.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

An Apple Watch series 12 and iPhone Duo are displayed at Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ event at the company’s corporate headquarters, Apple Park in Cupertino, California September 9, 2026. — Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images North America/Getty Images pic via AFP
Seven years later
Chinese competitors released their latest foldable products ahead of the Duo’s unveiling.
On Monday, Huawei unveiled its three-panel Mate XT 2, starting at 19,999 yuan (RM11,394), and Xiaomi unveiled its 18 Fold, starting at 10,999 yuan.
Samsung launched the industry’s first mainstream foldable smartphone, the Galaxy Fold, in 2019.

Foldable smartphones make up a tiny fraction of the market, at less than 2 per cent of global shipments, but Apple is expected to capture about a third of demand with its entry, according to research firm IDC.
“Apple’s foldable iPhone is very likely to shift the competitive dynamics both in China and global markets,” IDC research associate Kiranjeet Kaur told AFP.
The foldable iPhone’s release comes as demand for powerful chips amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom has created a supply chain crunch, pushing prices higher across industries.
As a result, smartphone shipments will decline by more than 16 per cent this year while the average cost jumps more than 27 per cent, according to IDC.

Apple also announced updated versions of its entry-level AirPods and smart watches, the latter of which will have improved heart-rate sensors that can be paired with an updated Health app launching later this year.

Other rumoured devices that did not get mentioned during yesterday’s event include an updated Apple TV box and HomePod mini speaker, as well as a smart home hub with a 7-inch screen, previously reported by Bloomberg. — AFP
5e6e8627d62cd51b: MANILA, Sept 10 — At least five people were killed and 87 remain unaccounted for after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan, the coast guard said Thursday.
The fire aboard the M/V June Aster broke out Wednesday evening about 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) offshore, the coast guard said, adding that five casualties had been brought ashore.
Video shared by the coast guard on Facebook showed the vessel completely engulfed in flames.

“Based on the data we have right now on rescued (42) and the casualties, we still have 87 people who are unaccounted for,” coast guard Captain Noemi Cayabyab told a local radio station on Thursday, adding the ship’s manifest had listed 134 passengers and crew.
“Just to make it clear, this is live data and may change as our search and rescue operations are ongoing,” she said.
Of those rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, Cayabyab said.
“However, we have not yet been able to obtain information from the rescued individuals because we have not been able to speak with them,” she said, adding attempts to put out the blaze were ongoing.
Tracking data from MarineTraffic showed the June Aster had departed from Manila. — AFP
531182f7f8a034aa: PORT KLANG, Sept 10 — The National Registration Department (NRD) disclosed that 365 foreigners were charged in court over MyKad and birth certificate fraud between January and August this year.

Enforcement director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said 738 joint operations were conducted with various agencies nationwide, including raids on premises and factories to detect the use of fraudulent identification documents.
“Of that number, 286 cases involved the use of fake identity cards or cards belonging to others, while another 79 were linked to forged birth certificates.
“Most of those arrested were Indonesian and Filipino nationals,” he told reporters after leading Ops Layar at a printing factory in Bandar Sultan Suleiman here last night.
Mazhad added that the prosecutions were carried out under the National Registration Regulations 1990 and the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957 (Act 299).
“We will continue to mount integrated and targeted enforcement operations to crack down on such activities,” he emphasised.

Meanwhile, he said Ops Layar, which ran for four hours starting at 5.00 pm, involved 52 NRD personnel from Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, as well as 15 officers from the Malaysian Immigration Department in Putrajaya and the Selangor Department of Labour.
“A total of 195 individuals were inspected, including 63 locals who were found to possess valid identity cards.

“Three women, aged between 21 and 37, believed to be Indonesian nationals, were detained on suspicion of using counterfeit identity cards or cards belonging to others to secure employment at the factory,” he said. — Bernama
13c92125d126a7e1: BATU PAHAT: A handyman was charged in the magistrate's court here today with threatening to kill his mother and burn down her house after she allegedly refused to give him RM2,500.
Muhammad Ashraf Sahridon, 26, pleaded not guilty to both charges before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
The unmarried accused allegedly threatened to cause the death of his 50-year-old mother and destroy her house in Jalan Parit Kemang, Senggarang, at 8.40am on Sept 6.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation, which carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both upon conviction.

Based on the police report, the accused went to his mother's house in an angry state and hurled abusive words at her before allegedly threatening: "Aku sembelih kau, kalau tak keluar, aku bakar rumah (I'll slash your throat, and if you don't come out, I'll burn the house)."
He allegedly made the threats after his mother refused his request for RM2,500.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Kamarulariffin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
The court granted a RM3,000 bail and fixed Sept 23 for mention for document submission and appointment of counsel.
8c1d34c2b734ae22: STEPPING into the spotlight as the child of a rock icon is rarely a simple affair, but newcomer Putri Aleeya Antasha is determined to forge her own identity without relying on her family legacy.

The 26-year-old actress, who is the daughter of legendary rocker Datuk Awie, clarified that her father maintains a professional outlook regarding her acting career, granting her full creative freedom even when navigating romantic scenes.
"Daddy understands how the industry works because we aren't doing this just for fun. There is no such thing as 'you can't do this or that' from him because he is incredibly professional," she said.

"My manager or I will usually explain details thoroughly to him, especially when working with new production houses. Beyond asking for his permission, I consult him to gauge if a storyline is suitable."
She added that Awie's core guidance focuses on artistic substance over rapid exposure.
"Daddy always advises me not to be greedy and to filter incoming offers. Rather than accepting everything, the priority should always be the quality of the work."
Taking that advice to heart, Putri Aleeya views her career as a continuous learning curve.
Her debut role in 'Dorm 403' served as a springboard that solidified her passion for the craft, opening doors to valuable industry networks and new experiences.
Moving forward, the rising talent is set to star in the upcoming vertical drama 'Hamza dan Mimi'.
Produced by Country & Universal Sdn Bhd, the series also features Zairi Aziz, Imranul Affendy, and Ako Mustapha.
It is scheduled to premiere on TV3 on Nov 7.
41f7b9ba785e8cc1: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Cement Bhd is well-positioned to weather potential coal supply disruptions from Indonesia, having secured sufficient stocks until November, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The YTL Group-controlled cement producer's share price has come under selling pressure since mid-August amid investor concerns over disruptions to coal supply and renewed tensions in the Middle East.

"Relative to the second half of August, the latest Indonesian benchmark prices for low- and medium-grade coal released for the first half of September actually softened by 1.1 per cent and 1.9 per cent, respectively.

"Furthermore, we posit that any price gains will likely be capped by softer demand from China and India — traditionally the top two buyers of Indonesian coal — as these markets are diversifying their sourcing by importing from other markets," CIMB Securities said in a note.
Malayan Cement aims to improve operating efficiency and increase its use of alternative fuels and materials to optimise production costs.
Its coal price assumption of US$90 per tonne for the financial years ending 2027 (FY27) and 2028 (FY28) remains above the spot price of US$83 per tonne for medium-grade Indonesian coal as at Sept 4.
CIMB Securities also expects domestic cement prices to remain fairly stable.
In the first seven months of 2026, domestic bag cement prices hovered within a narrow range of RM25.30 to RM25.95 per bag.
The research firm does not expect significant swings in cement prices for the rest of the year, provided there are no material changes in the trajectory of oil prices.
It maintained its "Buy" call on Malayan Cement with a target price of RM8.50.
Following the recent sharp pullback in the share price, CIMB Securities sees an increasingly attractive risk-reward profile for Malayan Cement.
The stock is trading at 12 times and 11 times its projected earnings for FY27 and FY28, respectively.
d321437251fa8708: NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 10 — Police discovered a man’s body at a house in Lorong 7, Taman Seri Bistari here today.
Seberang Perai Selatan deputy police chief DSP Mohd Norazmi Abd Ghapar said the deceased’s identity is being verified and a post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death.
“Police are conducting further investigations. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder,” he said in a statement last night.
He advised the public not to speculate or spread unverified information that could affect the investigation.
It is understood that the body, believed to be a man in his 50s, was found with hands and feet tied inside a sewage tank behind a single-storey terrace house near the kitchen.
The case is believed to be connected to a missing person’s report made on Sept 7. — Bernama
18d498a508423cbe: TEHRAN, Sept 10 — Iran said it attacked more than a dozen vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, as it announced an expansion of a no-go zone outside the strategic waterway it has blockaded for months.

The fresh attacks and fighting with the United States sent oil prices above US$100 (RM407) per barrel again as Tehran chokes off the strait and Washington presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Brent oil closed at US$101.21.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday they attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers, and 10 “non-compliant vessels” that were trying to pass through the route crucial for oil and gas trade, Iranian state media reported.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said “several” vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Gulf were “subject to disabling fire as part of ongoing military activity in the region”.
The Gulf of Oman lies on the Indian Ocean side of the narrow Hormuz strait, a vital energy conduit that normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas.
Iran’s Guards also for the first time added parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea to a new “prohibited zone” on Wednesday, saying exact coordinates will be announced later.
“If a vessel enters that area without coordination, it will be subject to our sanctions,” Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi told state television.
The Guards also said they struck a US military base in Jordan in response to US forces destroying five Iranian oil tankers a day earlier.
Jordan’s army shot down 18 missiles fired at the kingdom, it said.

Iran’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on its oil tankers as “an overt threat to regional and international peace and security,” saying the strikes “increase the dangers of tensions in the region”.
It said the targeting of US military facilities in the region was “self-defence”.
The US military for its part had said it was responding to an Iranian attack targeting an American warship, the second such incident in less than a week.
Long war?
Iran’s Guards, the ideological arm of the military, said the war could be brought to an end if Washington met its conditions, which included demands on the wars in Lebanon and Yemen.

“It must... refrain from renewed threats, withdraw the Israeli regime’s army from Lebanon, end the blockade of Yemen, release US$24 billion in Iran’s frozen assets and refrain from any interference in the country’s nuclear and missile capabilities,” Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.

Donald Trump, an unpopular president eager to end an unpopular war, asserted Wednesday the conflict will conclude right after the mid-term US elections in November. Polls show his Republican Party could face a drubbing and lose control of one or both houses of Congress.
“I think the war will end immediately after the election” because Iran “can’t hold out any longer,” Trump told journalists, accusing Tehran of being “desperate to try and affect” the vote.
However, the Wall Street Journal quoted US officials saying that Trump’s top advisers are privately warning that the war could drag on through the remaining two years of his term.
Nuclear referral

As Washington tries to choke off Iran economically, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) board of governors on Wednesday voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear “non-compliance”, in a diplomatic move that piles pressure on Tehran.
The resolution seen by AFP was adopted by a 23-3 vote with eight abstentions, they said. Russia, China and Niger voted against it.
Iran’s representative to the UN nuclear watchdog said the resolution was passed under US pressure, saying it “has no basis and will not bring any results”.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeated his claim Iran was about to collapse.
“The main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran. We are very close to that,” he said Wednesday on a troop visit in southern Syria, where Israel has occupied what it calls a “security zone”.
Tanker strikes

The latest round of US-Iran fighting was triggered after American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers Tuesday, with the US military saying it “directed the crews to abandon ship” before hitting the vessels.

“Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they’re going to lose tankers, and I think you’ll see that again today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters Tuesday on a visit to Colombia.
Iran has asserted control of the Strait of Hormuz since US-Israeli strikes began the war in February, with traffic through the waterway virtually paralysed.
Tehran requires vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the strait. — AFP
14216fd060515abc: KOTA BHARU, Sept 10 — The remains of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, one of five killed in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, are expected to be buried at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery here upon completion of forensic procedures.
Her father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said funeral prayers for Dr Ainul would be held at Masjid Al Karamah in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa.
“I have contacted the mosque management to make early preparations for the burial,” he told Bernama last night.
On when her remains would be flown from Miri to Kota Bharu, he said the matter had yet to be finalised.

Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) stated that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.
According to CAAM, the helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) mission when the incident occurred.

Meanwhile, Miri Division Resident Galong Luang, who is also Miri Division Disaster Management Committee chairman, confirmed that all five aboard the helicopter died in the crash at about 3.40 pm yesterday.

The victims were pilot Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama
fc87c8a9785a6157: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno will remain a centrist and moderate party and will not be pushed towards the political left or right, its deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today in an assurance to non-Malays and bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak.
Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said Umno’s ideology was rooted in centrism and that the party would continue to take the middle ground as a national party.
“My emphasis is that Umno will forever be centrist. Our ideology is centrism.

“Once again I repeat, Umno is a group and party of the middle and will forever follow the middle path,” he said in his speech at the simultaneous opening of the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri Umno general assemblies here last night.
He said Umno would not lean to the left or right, but would seek to balance ideas from both sides while remaining a moderate national party.
He said the party’s political position had been tested over decades through its experience in governing the country with moderate policies, positions and priorities.
“Therefore, anyone who wants to work with Umno must accept Umno’s moderation and centrist approach.
“You cannot impose your conservative or radical ideology on Umno,” he said.
Mohamad also sought to reassure non-Malays and non-Muslim bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak that Umno’s focus on Malay politics would not come at the expense of their rights and interests.
He said the Malays would continue to serve as the “indigenous nation” providing space and opportunities for everyone.
“We will ensure this homeland is a homeland for all, prosperous and carefully managed, in line with what is enshrined in the Federal Constitution,” he said.
Mohamad said Umno’s pledge was for a fair and united Malaysia, adding that the party would manage Malay politics maturely.
“It will in no way become a burden or threat, nor deny your rights and interests,” he said, addressing non-Malay friends and non-Muslim bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak.
He said Umno’s vision was for a peaceful Malaysia where all communities complemented one another.
fe9229bdcdcadb67: KLUANG, Sept 10 — A mother and her two sons were killed in a fire at a two-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa here last night.
The victims were identified as Noraini Ibrahim, 49, Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairulnizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadiff, 11.

The Johor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 10.44 pm before 14 personnel from the Kluang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene about five minutes later.
“The fire involved a two-storey terrace house measuring 16 feet by 70 feet, with about 50 per cent of the house’s structure engulfed in flames.
“There were three victims trapped inside the house, and all of them were confirmed dead by Health Ministry (MOH) personnel at the scene,” it said.
The fire was brought under control at 12.32 am.
The operation also involved two SITRAK fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit. — Bernama
dd37257349072da7: SINGAPORE, Sept 10 — Singapore’s largest bank, DBS Bank Ltd, said it is facing a lawsuit seeking damages estimated at S$1.30 billion (RM4.18 billion) in connection with 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).

In a statement on Wednesday, the bank said the lawsuit was filed by the liquidators of four companies, namely Affinity Equity International Partners Ltd, Blackrock Commodities (Global) Ltd, Platinum Global Luxury Services Ltd, and TKIL Global Investments Ltd.
The liquidators were Jason Aleksander Kardachi and Karnjote Singh s/o Jarmal Singh.
DBS said it has consulted its legal advisers, categorically rejects the claim, and will vigorously defend itself against the suit.
“It is a matter of public record that there have been global recovery efforts relating to 1MDB, supported by legal counsel since 2018.
“All this time, there was no claim against DBS,” the bank said, adding that it has assessed that no provisions are required at this stage. — Bernama
4107ccb9e08bbfd7: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarikei recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 194 as of 8am today, as 15 areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality amid the ongoing transboundary haze.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Sarawak dominating the unhealthy list, with 10 of the 15 locations in the state.

Serian recorded the second-highest API reading at 188, followed by Samarahan (181), Kuching (172), Samalaju (164), Sri Aman (158), Sibu (155), Mukah (153) and Bintulu (106), all of which were in the unhealthy range.
In the peninsula, Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 166, while Johor logged three unhealthy readings at Kluang (149), Larkin (146) and Batu Pahat (143), and one at Pasir Gudang (105).
Bukit Rambai in Melaka rounded out the unhealthy list at 104.

A wider band of areas was also inching close to the unhealthy threshold, with 22 locations in the Moderate category posting readings of 80 and above, just short of the 101 mark that would tip them into unhealthy territory.
Cheras in Kuala Lumpur led this group at 99, followed closely by Seremban (98), Alor Gajah (98), Tangkak (98) and Segamat (98), with Nilai (96), Pengerang (96) and Tasek Ipoh (95).
Johan Setia in Selangor (94) followed, along with Kota Tinggi (91), ILP Miri in Sarawak (90) and Putrajaya (88).

Also in the high-Moderate range were Balok Baru Kuantan (88), Jerantut (85), Tanjung Malim (84), Temerloh (84), Seri Manjung (83), Indera Mahkota Kuantan (83), Shah Alam (82), Banting (80), Bandaraya Melaka (80) and Kemaman (80).
Haze has gripped large parts of Sarawak since late August, with Serian earlier recording hazardous readings above 300 amid persistent hotspot activity in Kalimantan and Sumatra.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
The public can obtain the latest hourly API readings via the DOE website or the MyJAS EQMS mobile application.

d8ced578a1e39d9f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The ringgit held steady against the US dollar at Thursday’s opening as investors awaited the release of US consumer price index (CPI) data on Friday.
At 8am, the local currency was unchanged at 4.0670/0720 against the greenback from Wednesday’s close.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US CPI data would influence expectations for the United States Federal Reserve’s interest rate path and could weigh on market sentiment.
“There seems to be less catalyst for a stronger ringgit, especially as traders will be watching the US CPI print to be published on Friday.

“At the same time, it is a risk-off environment and traders are seeking refuge from market volatility amid higher crude oil prices. Hence, we expect the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade within a range of RM4.05 to RM4.07 today,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said Brent crude oil prices were hovering at US$101.21 (RM411.83) a barrel as tensions between the United States and Iran were expected to escalate.
The ringgit traded lower against most major currencies.

It slipped against the Japanese yen to 2.6483/6519 from 2.6474/6509 at Wednesday’s close, fell against the euro to 4.7311/7370 from 4.7275/7333, and eased against the British pound to 5.5100/5167 from 5.5043/5110.
Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.

It edged up against the Thai baht to 12.3459/3675 from 12.3579/3788 at the previous close, while it was unchanged against the Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah at 6.50/6.52 and 232.2/232.6, respectively.
However, the local note softened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2165/2210 from 3.2150/2192 previously. — Bernama
8deb54ed23ae24e9: KLUANG: A shortage of manpower is putting pressure on Enche' Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital here as its bed capacity and specialist services expand to meet the needs of more than 330,000 people.

Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the hospital currently has 396 beds, with another 38 expected to be added once Ward 10B upgrading works are completed by the end of September.

"However, the hospital is now facing a shortage of manpower. Specialist services and the number of beds increased, but the workforce has not been expanded in tandem," he said following a working visit to the hospital.
Ling said some wards are currently being upgraded with full air-conditioning.
"Johor will be raising the medical assistance manpower shortages with the health ministry.
The hospital plays an important role in providing healthcare services to the Kluang district's more than 330,000 residents, he said.

639f8035ff8478f3: NEW YORK: Elena Rybakina ended Zheng Qinwen's spirited US Open run with a three-set victory on Wednesday, ensuring she'll rise to number one in the world for the first time.
The 27-year-old Kazakh star beat Zheng 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 and booked a clash with former champion Coco Gauff for a place in the title match.
Men's top seed Alexander Zverev was also gunning for a semi-final spot on Wednesday, taking on Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp.
World number two Rybakina was assured of ending Aryna Sabalenka's reign at number one just by reaching the semis – even if Sabalenka wins a third straight title.
"It's just a number right now," Rybakina said. "It's a different achievement ... but mostly you think about the titles in the end of the day."

Gauff, who won the first of her two major titles at Flushing Meadows in 2023, saved two match points in a 2-6, 7-6 (9/7), 6-2 victory over Russian 19-year-old Mirra Andreeva, the fifth-ranked reigning French Open champion from Russia.
"Elena is the new world number one," Gauff said. "It's going to be a tough match. These are the moments you live for."
Gauff struggled early, withstood two match points in the tie-break then rallied with some inspiration from Frances Tiafoe's come-from-behind five-set victory over fellow American Alex Michelsen.
"I just had to reset," Gauff said. "Honestly, I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back. I was just trying to leave the court without regrets."

In van de Zandschulp he could face a trickier proposition than the Dutch player's number 70 ranking implies. Van de Zandschulp famously toppled Carlos Alcaraz in the second round two years ago and sent sixth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur packing in the second round last week.

e0a50b6b6ff3421a: KUALA LUMPUR: The Embassy of Malaysia in Addis Ababa received a high-level Ethiopian delegation on Tuesday for a courtesy visit, reflecting the positive bilateral engagement between the two countries ahead of Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year.

The embassy, in a statement to Bernama, said the delegation comprised representatives from various Ethiopian ministries, which include Foreign Affairs, Tourism and Culture and Sport, as well as the Ethiopian News Agency.
Representing the Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Amha Hailegeorgis conveyed the Ethiopian Government's New Year greetings to the Malaysian mission.
"The visit reflects the mutual respect that continues to underpin relations between the two countries," he said.

Malaysia's Chargé d'Affaires Mohd Afandi Abu Bakar thanked the delegation for the gesture and extended his wishes to Ethiopians at home and abroad for a peaceful and prosperous Ethiopian New Year 2019.
He described the visit as a reflection of the friendship built between the two nations over the past year.

According to the statement, the courtesy call also featured an exchange of cultural traditions. The Ethiopian delegation presented Abebayehosh singing, kebero drum performances, and the yellow Adey Abeba flower, with performers dressed in traditional Habesha kemis.
The embassy reciprocated with a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony and freshly made anababero, alongside Malaysian dishes including kuih kasturi and pulut kuning serunding.
The yellow hue of the pulut kuning was chosen to echo the Adey Abeba flower, in keeping with the New Year's themes of renewal, the statement added.

The statement said, the visit came almost exactly a year after Malaysia's first diplomatic team arrived in Addis Ababa to reopen the embassy, marking a year of growing bilateral engagement between the two countries.
Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year, falls on Sept 11 under the Ethiopian calendar, which has 13 months and runs roughly seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
This year's celebration marks the start of the Ethiopian year 2019.

“Look at how Umno has tried to justify and explain its cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government.
“There is no argument that can convince the majority of the Malay constituency, or soften their position, to accept Umno’s cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government.

“However, all this is not seen as being more Malay.

ce97910e630a9521: THE 2026 Umno general assembly, being held at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur from yesterday till Saturday, is expected to see more than 6,400 delegates across the main assembly and the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri wings.
Pre-assembly programmes have already addressed Islamic scholarship, Malay education, women, artificial intelligence and the digital economy.
The setting combines tradition with an attempt to frame Umno's relevance around social and technological change.
The political message is one of consolidation before expansion.
Party leaders have repeatedly described the assembly as a forum for introspection, organisational unity and preparation for the 16th General Election.
Grassroots voices gathered through branch meetings and all 191 divisions are being presented as an essential input into strategy.

This emphasis reflects a lesson from Umno's experience: electoral recovery cannot be managed solely from headquarters. Candidate credibility, local organisation, constituency-specific alliances and disciplined service delivery determine whether national branding converts into votes.

Coalition strategy remains a sensitive variable. Umno's supreme council has authorised state leaders to negotiate political cooperation with parties interested in working together at the next election, provided negotiations rest on sincerity and trust rather than pressure.
Pas leaders were also invited to the general assembly.
These developments do not establish a new national pact, but they demonstrate strategic flexibility.

Umno is attempting to preserve room for state-specific arrangements while protecting its leverage inside Malaysia's coalition system, a difficult balance between ideological familiarity, electoral arithmetic and governmental stability.
The Rumah Bangsa narrative seeks to provide an organising frame for Malay political consolidation without reducing the party's future to nostalgia.
Its effectiveness will depend on whether unity is translated into governance outcomes.

Malay voters face concerns involving incomes, education, housing, employment opportunities, social mobility and the cost of living. A revival strategy built on emotional solidarity would be insufficient.
For Umno, political identity must be connected to economic competence, credible institutions and measurable improvements in everyday life.

Governance and integrity remain tests. Shortly before the assembly, the party leadership reaffirmed the rule of law, stating that wrongdoing should not be defended and that members or leaders must face due legal process.
Such language is important, but its political value depends on consistent application.

Umno's challenge is not to communicate integrity; it is to institutionalise transparent standards for candidate selection, accountability, political financing, internal discipline and performance evaluation. Public trust is rebuilt through evidence, not declarations alone.

Generational change presents strategic pressure. The pre-assembly focus on education, artificial intelligence, digital communication and technology indicates recognition that younger Malaysians inhabit a political information environment.

Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remarks on scholars understanding algorithms, social media and artificial intelligence, alongside his support for student intellectual participation, illustrate this shift.

Yet digital modernisation cannot mean better propaganda alone. It requires faster policy feedback, credible data, professional communication and leadership capable of engaging sceptical voters who compare claims instantly across competing platforms.

Economically, Umno's opportunity is to reconnect political representation with material security. Stability, investment confidence and national development remain important, but voters experience the economy through wages, prices, jobs, household debt and access to opportunity.
The party's institutional experience gives it an advantage in discussing administration and development, but that legacy becomes useful only when converted into contemporary solutions.
Policy credibility will require clear priorities, financing discipline, implementation timelines and measurable outcomes rather than broad promises.
As the assembly takes place, the available evidence points less to a completed transformation than to incremental recalibration.

Umno is signalling openness to localised coalition strategy, stronger grassroots consultation, renewed Malay political consolidation, technological adaptation and a more explicit governance narrative.

Its strengths remain organisational reach, institutional memory and an experienced leadership network; its weaknesses include credibility deficits, internal tensions and the risk that reform language outruns implementation.
The evidence will emerge during the proceedings, the presidential policy speech, wing debates, resolutions and closing commitments.
The research gap is temporal as well as institutional: the assembly has not yet concluded, so any definitive verdict would be premature.
The test will come afterward, when resolutions can be tracked against decisions, electoral strategy and policy delivery.

On evidence, the general assembly is best understood as an exercise in strategic recalibration with renewal ambitions, whose substance must still be demonstrated through implementation in the months that follow.

74dd8ee25e68f33d: Kita semua berasa hairan dengan sikap sesetengah pembesar adat di Negeri Sembilan, terutama dari Johol, Jelebu dan Tampin yang tidak sudah-sudah bertikai, dan sekali lagi cuba menurunkan penyandang semasa Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan iaitu Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir yang memegang takhta sejak 29 Dis 2008.

Sehingga hari ini kita masih belum tahu apakah punca dan motif mereka tergamak menodai kesakralan adat tanpa segan silu. Jembalang utara, atau selatan yang manakah di belakang mereka sehingga seberani ini menderhakai Raja Berkeadilan?

Mohd Rais Yatim, pengerusi Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) yang merupakan salah satu parti komponen dalam Perikatan Nasional dan kini bekerjasama dengan Umno kelihatan tampil sebagai ‘pakar adat mereka’. Rais yang mengaku ‘pakar adat’ ini ada menukil bagaimana Adat Perpatih harus diperlakukan. Beliau menulis begini:
“When adat was the prime mover of social modus operandi in Minangkabau prior to the Pasumpahan Satie Bukik Marapalam in about 1838, the common and effective philosophy was thus:
Mamak basanda ka Pangulu Pangulu basanda ka mupakaik Mupakaik basanda ka nan bana Nan bana tagak sandirinyo

This is to say 'the mamak relies on the Pengulu who in turn relies on the rule of consensus and consensus stands on what is the truth and the truth stands on its own. It could also be argued in extension that now the system no longer relies on the truth or what is just and fair. It simply relies on the Book (the Quran) which in turn of course excretes justice and fairness. And so the shift to over-reliance on religion is the preferred mode rather than on the priority and impetus of relying on what is the truth or the just and fair disposition. The Musa Wahab case is now a milestone decision. It now settles two issues: first, the courts have no jurisdiction in adjudicating matters pertaining to the business of Undang or an adat leader succession! Second, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang may have the prerogative of giving a blessing or otherwise in an Undangship claim. Curiously, this decision should have relied more on the force of Art. 14 of the state Constitution which states that the business of adat leadership succession should be left to the device "...in accordance with the custom of their respective luaks". The fact that more weight is given to the blessing of the Dewan has become a new yardstick hence the introduction of a new provision under Art 16(2) somewhat gives the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang a new constitutional assertion. It would appear that in future whenever the Dewan gives its blessings' the Undang candidate in a luak could mean an endorsement and this act could also mean as an interference contrary to Art. 14 of the State Constitution.”

Petikan panjang di atas terdapat dalam ‘Adat The Legacy of Minangkabau’ terbitan 2015 oleh Rais Yatim. Untuk memudahkan pembesar dan sesetengah mereka yang berdegil untuk terus berkelahi perihal kuasa ini, izinkan saya terjemahkan petikan di atas ke dalam bahasa Melayu, pandai-pandailah membacanya dalam dialek Negori:
“Apabila adat menjadi penggerak utama modus operandi sosial di Minangkabau sebelum berlakunya Pasumpahan Satie Bukik Marapalam sekitar tahun 1838, falsafah yang lazim dan berkesan adalah:
Mamak basanda ka Pangulu Pangulu basanda ka mupakaik Mupakaik basanda ka nan bana Nan bana tagak sandirinyo

Ini bermaksud bahawa mamak bersandar kepada penghulu, penghulu pula bersandar kepada keputusan muafakat, muafakat bersandarkan kepada kebenaran, dan kebenaran berdiri atas kekuatannya sendiri. Boleh juga dihujahkan bahawa kini sistem tersebut tidak lagi bersandar kepada kebenaran, atau apa yang adil dan saksama. Sebaliknya, ia semata-mata bersandar kepada Kitab, iaitu al-Quran, yang kemudiannya dianggap sebagai sumber keadilan dan kesaksamaan. Dengan demikian, berlaku suatu peralihan kepada kebergantungan yang berlebihan kepada agama, menggantikan keutamaan dan dorongan untuk berpaut kepada apa yang benar, adil dan saksama. Kes Musa Wahab kini menjadi suatu keputusan penting (milestone decision). Ia menetapkan dua perkara.
Pertama, mahkamah tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa untuk mengadili perkara yang berkaitan dengan urusan Undang atau pewarisan jawatan pemimpin adat.

Kedua, Dewan Keadilan dan Undang mempunyai prerogatif untuk memberikan perkenan atau sebaliknya terhadap tuntutan seseorang untuk menjadi Undang. Menariknya, keputusan ini sepatutnya lebih banyak bersandar pada kuasa dan maksud Perkara 14 Perlembagaan Negeri, yang menyatakan bahawa urusan pewarisan kepimpinan adat hendaklah diserahkan kepada mekanisme: “…in accordance with the custom of their respective luaks” (“…mengikut adat bagi luak masing-masing.”) Hakikat bahawa 'perkenan' Dewan diberikan lebih banyak pertimbangan telah menjadi suatu ukuran baharu. Hal ini kemudiannya dapat dilihat melalui pengenalan Perkara 16(2), yang seolah-olah memberikan kepada Dewan Keadilan dan Undang suatu kedudukan atau penegasan perlembagaan yang baharu. Nampaknya, pada masa hadapan, apabila Dewan memberikan 'perkenan' kepada calon Undang dalam sesuatu luak, perkenan tersebut boleh ditafsirkan sebagai suatu bentuk pengesahan atau sokongan.”

Baca beberapa kali biar teliti. Adalah jelas terang lagi bersuluh, bersiap huraian di atas, Rais sendiri sedar halnya. Dewan Keadilan adalah kini kuasa pengesah dalam menentukan kedudukan seseorang Undang. Ia juga tidak wajar dicabar di Mahkamah. Dan yang paling penting, Rais Yatim sendiri memutuskan bahawa setiap sesuatu itu mestilah dibuat menurut keadilan dan tentulah itu bermuarakan agama Islam.
Islam celah mana yang mereka ingin tunggang sebagai hujah? Adakah Baginda Tuanku Muhriz sudah diberi keadilan?

Dari segi adat juga, untuk menurunkan Yamtuan Besar, seorang Undang itu sendiri mesti sah di Luak masing-masing. Kita telah pun tahu duduk letak Undang di Luak Sungei Ujong, Rembau, Jelebu dalam keadaan penuh pertikaian. Malah mereka sudah dipecat oleh Waris, dan ditolak pembesar adat yang kanan di wilayah masing-masing.
Undang Sungei Ujong dan Rembau yang baru, kedua-duanya menyokong Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir. Datuk Klana Petra, Muhammad Faris Johari telah dimasyhurkan dan dizahirkan sebagai Undang.

Luak Sungai Ujong ke-11 pada Mei dan Jun 2026.Dari segi adat Mubarak Dohak telah lama ditolak. Manakala Hassan Ab Hamid telah dizahirkan sebagai Undang Luak Rembau ke-22 pada Jun 2026 berikutan adat istiadat yang sah di negeri tersebut. Beliau bersama-sama Undang Sungai Ujong telah menegaskan pendirian rasmi Luak masing-masing berkaitan hal ehwal istana dan adat di Negeri Sembilan termasuklah kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan.
Jadi celah mana yang Umno, Rais berserta segala jembalang baik utara atau selatan tidak faham?

Ternyata kerajaan Negeri Sembilan yang baru, yang turut disertai oleh Wawasan tidak mampu menyelesaikan masalah atau krisis kepimpinan adat. Menggunakan lojik mereka sebelum pilihan raya negeri, mereka wajar meletakkan jawatan semuanya. Lebih menghairankan, siapakah di belakang mereka? Jembalang Utara? Jembalang Selatan? Jembalang mana yang mendanai segala kudrat dan tenaga mereka ini?
Aduh, berhentilah menjahat sepenggal, biar kita-kita aman dari sakau.

Dan ya untuk menurunkan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, kita mesti tahu punca dan motifnya. Sampai hari ini, setelah gegak gempita alam dan berlaku pilihan raya negeri yang penuh fitnah dan persepsi, kita masih ternanti-nanti apa asbabnya?

340689bcef6bd3f0: SEVILLE, Spain: Sprint king Matthew Brennan claimed a fifth Vuelta a Espana stage victory on Wednesday as he edged a bunch sprint in Seville to win the 17th stage.
The 21-year-old Grand Tour debutant crossed the finish line ahead of Jordi Meeus and Magnus Cort Nielsen.

General classification leader Enric Mas moved one step closer to claiming a first Grand Tour victory as he maintained his 2min 6sec lead on Felix Gall, with four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic a further four seconds behind.
The stage was set up for the bunch sprint finale, without a single climb on the long, flat, 185 kilometre ride from Dos Hermanas to the Andalusian capital.

Sinuhe Fernandez and Enzo Paleni formed a two-man break early on, whipping up a gap of more than four minutes on the peloton, who were moving at a leisurely pace on another hot day with temperatures over 30C.
The gap extended to over five minutes around the halfway point, with Visma then working hard to reduce it.
Groupama FDJ-United rider Paleni dropped Fernandez but was absorbed by the peloton with just three kilometres remaining after a monumental effort.
Young star Brennan came around Danish rider Cort to claim the sprint victory, holding off Belgium's Meeus who crossed the line second.
As with his other stage victories, the Briton raised his hand to the air, this time with all of his fingers up to represent his five victories.

Brennan's victory puts him in a small bracket of riders, including Tadej Pogacar – who was overwhelming favourite to win this year's Vuelta before he suffered a season-ending injury in a crash in stage eight – to claim five or more stages at a single Grand Tour.

On Thursday, riders take on a 32.1km individual time-trial from El Puerto de Santa Maria to Jerez de la Frontera in stage 18, which is one of the last chances for Mas's general classification contenders to cut down the gap on the Spaniard.
0587cdd7b6dbf9e0: SHAH ALAM: Bagi Ahmad Fitri Mohd Nor, 23, peluang melanjutkan pengajian ke peringkat Ijazah Sarjana Muda Kejuruteraan Elektronik di Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) hadir bersama cabaran mengurus kos sara hidup yang semakin meningkat.
Anak keenam daripada lapan beradik itu pada mulanya bercadang mencari kerja sambilan bagi menampung perbelanjaan sepanjang pengajian.
Namun, perancangannya berubah selepas terpilih menerima Inisiatif Biasiswa Anak eKasih PTPTN (BAeK PTPTN) berjumlah RM26,600.

BAeK PTPTN merupakan inisiatif bersasar Kerajaan dalam menyediakan pendidikan percuma kepada pelajar daripada keluarga miskin dan miskin tegar. Inisiatif ini dilaksanakan sebagai pendekatan keadilan sosial bagi memperluaskan akses kepada pendidikan tinggi.

Melalui BAeK PTPTN, pembiayaan pendidikan yang ditawarkan oleh PTPTN diberikan dalam bentuk biasiswa kepada pelajar yang mengikuti pengajian sepenuh masa di peringkat Diploma atau Ijazah Sarjana Muda di IPTA yang diluluskan pinjaman PTPTN mulai 1 Januari 2026.
Bagi Ahmad Fitri Mohd Nor melalui inisiatif yang diterimanya ini membolehkannya menumpukan sepenuh perhatian kepada pelajaran tanpa perlu memikirkan komitmen kerja sambilan.
“Saya tidak perlu lagi memikirkan tentang kerja sambilan dan boleh memberi fokus sepenuhnya terhadap pengajian.
“Dalam jangka panjang, penukaran pinjaman kepada biasiswa ini juga membolehkan saya menamatkan pengajian tanpa dibebani hutang,” katanya kepada FMT.
Katanya, individu pertama yang dihubunginya untuk berkongsi berita gembira itu ialah ibunya.
“Selepas saya jelaskan bahawa pinjaman itu ditukar kepada biasiswa, ibu sangat bersyukur kerana nilainya amat besar bagi keluarga kami,” katanya.

Kelegaan sama dirasai Irwana Mahad, 22, pelajar Ijazah Sarjana Muda Pengurusan Sumber Manusia di UiTM Puncak Alam yang menerima biasiswa untuk membiayai hampir keseluruhan yuran asas pengajiannya berjumlah RM18,000.
Menurutnya, bantuan itu digunakan untuk menampung yuran pengajian, sewa kolej, kos sara hidup dan pembelian buku rujukan.
Sebelum menerima BAeK PTPTN, Irwana bekerja sambilan ketika cuti semester untuk memperoleh pendapatan tambahan.
Namun, biasiswa itu kini memberinya ruang untuk memberi tumpuan kepada pelajaran tanpa terlalu bimbang mengenai kedudukan kewangan keluarga.
“Ibu bapa berpesan supaya saya tidak sia-siakan peluang ini dan terus belajar bersungguh-sungguh. Walaupun biasiswa ini tidak perlu dibayar balik, mereka mengingatkan saya supaya tidak leka.
“Usaha Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan PTPTN ini amat baik kerana pelajar dapat fokus belajar tanpa perlu memikirkan masalah kewangan atau komitmen hutang selepas tamat pengajian,” katanya.
Membuka peluang pendidikan tinggi

BAeK PTPTN diperkenalkan bagi memastikan faktor kewangan tidak menjadi penghalang kepada pelajar daripada keluarga miskin dan miskin tegar untuk melanjutkan pengajian di Institusi Pendidikan Tinggi Awam (IPTA).

Menerusi inisiatif ini, pinjaman PTPTN diberikan dalam bentuk biasiswa kepada pelajar daripada keluarga yang berdaftar dalam pangkalan data ekasih, tertakluk kepada syarat yang ditetapkan. Terdahulu, menerusi Belanjawan 2026 mengumumkan inisiatif biasiswa/pendidikan percuma PTPTN untuk 5,800 anak-anak keluarga miskin yang mengikuti pengajian di Institusi Pendidikan Tinggi Awam dengan peruntukan RM120 juta setahun.
Semasa pelancaran Rancangan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia (RPTM) 2026 2035, jumlah penerima ini telah ditingkatkan kepada 10,000 orang pelajar.

BaeK ditawarkan kepada pelajar Malaysia berusia tidak melebihi 25 tahun pada tarikh permohonan, kursus diikuti berdaftar dengan PTPTN, mempunyai akaun Simpan SSPN yang masih aktif, tiada tunggakan pinjaman PTPTN dan baki tempoh pengajian semasa membuat permohonan tidak kurang daripada satu semester.
Melalui pelaksanaan BAeK PTPTN, pelajar akan ditawarkan biasiswa mengikut jumlah/ kadar pinjaman yang layak diterima.
Inisiatif itu membuktikan komitmen dan keprihatinan kerajaan dalam memastikan latar belakang sosioekonomi bukan penghalang kepada peluang melanjutkan pengajian ke peringkat lebih tinggi.

652073e8af29fe51: SHAH ALAM: For 23-year-old Ahmad Fitri Nor, pursuing a degree in electronic engineering at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) meant finding a way to cope with rising living costs while keeping up with his studies.

"In the long run, having my loan converted into a scholarship also means I can graduate without being burdened by debt," he told FMT.

Fitri said the first person he called with the good news was his mother. "Once I explained that the loan had been converted into a scholarship, my mother was extremely grateful because it means so much to our family."
For 22-year-old Irwana Mahad, a Bachelor of Human Resource Management student at UiTM Puncak Alam, the scholarship also translates into sheer relief.
She received about RM18,000 to cover her basic tuition fees and said the financial assistance would also help with accommodation, living expenses and reference books.
Before receiving the BAeK PTPTN scholarship, Irwana worked part-time during semester breaks to supplement her income.
She said the assistance would now allow her to focus more fully on her studies without worrying as much about her family's financial situation.
"My parents reminded me not to waste this opportunity and to continue studying hard. Although the scholarship does not have to be repaid, they also reminded me not to become complacent.

"This initiative by the higher education ministry and PTPTN is excellent because it allows students to focus on their studies without worrying about financial problems or repaying loans after graduation."
BAeK PTPTN was introduced to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent students from poor and hardcore poor families from pursuing higher education at public institutions.

Through BAeK PTPTN, PTPTN education financing is provided in the form of scholarships to students pursuing full-time Diploma or Bachelor’s Degree programmes at public higher education institutions, who have been approved to receive PTPTN loans from Jan 1 2026.
The initiative was first announced under the 2026 Budget, which allocated RM120 million annually to convert standard loans into free scholarships for 5,800 students from poor families.
When launching the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint 2026-2035, the government increased the target to benefit 10,000 recipients.

Eligible recipients must be Malaysian citizens aged 25 and below at the time of application, enrolled in PTPTN-approved programmes, have an active Simpan SSPN account, have no outstanding PTPTN loan arrears and have at least one semester remaining when they apply.
Through the implementation of the PTPTN BAeK scheme, students will be offered a scholarship based on the loan amount or rate for which they are eligible.
The initiative reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that a student's socioeconomic background of hardship does not become a barrier in the pursuit of higher education.
For more information, visit www.ptptn.gov.my.

0f3a53e73e82649b: The famous observation that "power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely" is particularly relevant in the business world.

Power is necessary for organisations to function. Directors need authority to make strategic decisions, chief executives need power to allocate resources, and managers need sufficient authority to lead their teams.
However, when power becomes concentrated, unchecked or exercised without accountability, it can gradually undermine judgement, ethics, governance and ultimately the organisation itself.
Power does not necessarily corrupt everyone who possesses it. Rather, unchecked power can create an environment in which poor behaviour becomes easier, less visible and less likely to be challenged.
The greater the authority and the weaker the controls surrounding it, the greater the risk of abuse.
The concentration of power

One of the most significant governance risks in business is excessive concentration of power in one individual or a small group. This may occur when a founder, dominant shareholder, chairman, chief executive or family owner controls most important decisions.

Initially, concentration of power may appear beneficial. Decisions can be made quickly, bureaucracy can be avoided and the organisation can pursue a clear strategic direction. However, over time, the same concentration can create serious weaknesses.
When one individual becomes too powerful, others may become reluctant to challenge that person's decisions. Directors may become dependent on the chief executive.
Senior managers may tell the leader what they want to hear rather than what they need to hear. Employees may fear retaliation if they question questionable decisions.
The result is an organisation where authority becomes stronger than accountability.
Power can change behaviour
Power can gradually change how individuals perceive themselves and others. A successful executive may begin to believe that past achievements demonstrate superior judgement in every situation.
Confidence can turn into arrogance, and strong leadership can become authoritarian leadership.

A powerful executive may begin to believe that rules are applicable to others but not to themselves. Expenses may be treated as personal privileges, conflicts of interest may be ignored, related-party transactions may receive inadequate scrutiny, and corporate resources may be used for personal benefit.

The danger is that misconduct rarely begins with a major fraud. It can begin with relatively small exceptions: approving an unusual expense, bypassing a procurement procedure, overriding a control or asking employees to conceal unfavourable information.
If these actions are tolerated, the boundaries of acceptable behaviour gradually move.
Absolute power destroys challenge
Perhaps the greatest danger of excessive power is the destruction of constructive challenge.

Good corporate governance requires directors and executives to question assumptions, examine risks and challenge decisions. A healthy board does not simply endorse management proposals. It asks difficult questions.

But when a dominant executive controls information, influences board appointments or intimidates dissenters, independent challenge can disappear. Board meetings may become formalities rather than genuine decision-making forums.

This creates the dangerous phenomenon of groupthink. Directors may convince themselves that supporting the dominant leader is safer than challenging the leader. Eventually, everyone agrees—and nobody is truly thinking independently.
Many corporate failures demonstrate that the problem is not always the absence of information. Sometimes the information exists, but nobody is willing to challenge the person who possesses the power.
Power and financial manipulation
The relationship between excessive power and financial misconduct is particularly important.

Executives under pressure to meet earnings targets, maintain share prices or demonstrate growth may manipulate accounting estimates, accelerate revenue recognition, defer expenses or conceal liabilities.
If the CEO is sufficiently powerful, finance personnel and auditors may find it difficult to resist management pressure.
A culture can therefore develop where financial reporting becomes an instrument for protecting management's reputation rather than providing objective information to shareholders.
This is why an effective audit committee, independent directors and strong internal audit function are so important. They provide additional layers of challenge and accountability.
The role of the board

The board is one of the most important safeguards against the misuse of executive power. Directors must be prepared to challenge management, particularly when decisions involve significant financial, strategic or reputational risks.
This requires genuine independence—not merely formal independence.

An independent director who is unwilling to challenge management provides little protection. Similarly, a board may appear sophisticated on paper but remain ineffective if directors are overly dependent on management information or relationships.
The board must therefore create an environment where disagreement is acceptable. A director should not be regarded as disloyal merely because he or she asks difficult questions.
Indeed, constructive disagreement is one of the board's most valuable contributions.
Controls are necessary—but culture matters too
Internal controls, segregation of duties, approval limits, whistleblowing mechanisms and audit procedures can help prevent abuse of power. However, controls alone are insufficient.

If the organisational culture rewards results regardless of how those results are achieved, employees may find ways around controls. If senior executives routinely override procedures, employees quickly learn that policies are merely suggestions.
The strongest control is therefore a combination of ethical leadership, independent oversight and effective systems of accountability.
The tone at the top matters enormously. Employees watch what leaders do, not merely what leaders say.
The danger of unchecked success

Ironically, successful organisations may be particularly vulnerable. A leader who has delivered extraordinary growth may accumulate enormous influence. The board may hesitate to challenge someone regarded as indispensable.
Past success can therefore become a source of future risk.
The question should never be, "Has this person been successful?" It should be, "What happens if this person's judgement is wrong, and who has the authority to challenge it?"
No individual, however talented, should become more important than the governance system protecting the organisation.

7cfadde345c08685: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's data centre boom is spreading deeper into the economy, creating new opportunities across construction, power infrastructure and the technology supply chain, analysts said.

It is estimated that Malaysia's data centre capacity could reach eight to nine gigawatts (GW) by 2030, creating a RM128 billion to RM162 billion market for the domestic mechanical and electrical (M&E) sector.

CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said about 3.8GW is already under construction or backed by signed electricity supply agreements, while another 4GW to 5GW of incremental demand is expected by the end of the decade.
The ripple effect is also being felt elsewhere in the technology ecosystem, with company earnings tracked by RHB Research more than tripling in the second quarter on stronger factory loadings.
At the same time, contractors involved in the power infrastructure needed for data centres are seeing their project pipelines grow.
THE BUILDING BLOCKS
For the construction industry, much of the opportunity lies in the M&E works needed to keep increasingly power-hungry data centres running.
CIMB Securities estimates the capital value of M&E equipment and construction at US$4 million to US$4.5 million for every megawatt (MW) of capacity, equivalent to RM16 million to RM18 million per MW.
While the cost per MW has remained broadly stable since the start of the data centre boom, rising power intensity from changing server architecture is resulting in larger job awards.
Localisation policies are also opening the door to greater domestic participation, creating opportunities for local subcontractors and equipment manufacturers.
CIMB Securities said local companies have an advantage in navigating domestic regulatory requirements.
But the growing pie is attracting more players. A shortage of large-scale infrastructure projects elsewhere has pushed more well-funded contractors into the data centre market.
Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd is among the latest entrants, having secured an RM858 million mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out contract for a data centre in Iskandar Puteri.
Some contractors are going a step further by developing data centre campuses together with their utility infrastructure.
CIMB Securities said this could lower execution risks for clients and improve the chances of contractors securing repeat work.
The research house maintained its "Neutral" call on the construction sector, but described the domestic data centre pipeline as a silver lining.
It retained "Buy" calls on Gamuda Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd for selective exposure to the sector.

Gamuda has about RM7 billion of data centre wins from its Springhill data centre campus. CIMB Securities said IJM, meanwhile, is supported by restructuring, potential dividend upside and earnings visibility from data centre progress billings.
But building and fitting out data centres is only part of the equation. They also need huge amounts of electricity, bringing Malaysia's power infrastructure into the picture.
POWERING THE BOOM

Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) believes Malaysia's power infrastructure cycle is building faster than expected, driven by data centres, Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) capital expenditure and solar projects.
The growing pipeline can be seen at MN Holdings Bhd, whose tenderbook has reached a record RM5 billion. Tenders linked to TNB, data centres and solar projects are all at record highs.
Its existing order book stands at RM1.6 billion, providing visibility against HLIB's financial year 2027 (FY27) revenue forecast of RM1.2 billion.
HLIB expects about RM1 billion of data centre and solar projects to be recognised during the year.
More could be coming down the pipeline.
Separately, HLIB said the Data Centre Task Force had approved an additional 5GW of capacity on top of what it described as an existing 8.3GW.
If the projects progress to electricity supply agreement signings in 2027, the research house expects a significant increase in project awards in 2027 and 2028.
For MN Holdings alone, the data centre tender pipeline stands at RM1.6 billion, including about RM500 million linked to a major customer.
The remainder largely comprises one underground utilities engineering project and three new data centre developments.

Data centres, however, are not the only game in town. MN Holdings' solar tenderbook has reached a record RM400 million, while TNB still has a sizeable portion of its FY26 regulated capital expenditure programme to deploy.
The utility had spent RM5.6 billion of its RM13 billion target at the time of HLIB's report.
Large transmission projects are also adding to the pipeline. Two 500-kilovolt (kV) projects at Pakas and Ujong Pasir account for about RM1.5 billion of MN Holdings' TNB tenderbook.
Another RM1 billion comes from 132kV and 275kV projects.
HLIB's channel checks point to more 500kV projects coming to market, with another seven potentially being launched from 2027 onwards.
The research house maintained its "Buy" call on MN Holdings and raised its target price to RM4.65, reflecting the faster build-up in power infrastructure demand.
EARNINGS MORE THAN TRIPLE
While contractors prepare for the next wave of infrastructure spending, Malaysia's technology companies are already seeing an earnings recovery take shape.
Aggregate core earnings among the 12 companies tracked by RHB Research surged 206 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM154.5 million in the second quarter from RM50.5 million previously.

But the headline number masks an uneven recovery. Aggregate earnings were still 25.8 per cent lower than a year earlier, dragged mainly by weakness among electronic manufacturing services (EMS) players.
Strip out the EMS outliers, and sector earnings rose 21.7 per cent year-on-year, reflecting what RHB Research described as a broad-based recovery and semiconductor upcycle.
Eight of the 12 companies delivered earnings within expectations, the firm said. Inari Amertron Bhd and Cnergenz Bhd were the key outperformers on stronger revenue and margins.
On the flip side, SKP Resources Bhd and VS Industry Bhd missed forecasts due to weaker-than-expected revenue and margins, an unfavourable product mix and higher input costs.
RHB Research cut its overall FY26 technology sector earnings forecast by 2.8 per cent, mainly due to weaker projections for SKP Resources and VS Industry.
Excluding EMS players, however, it raised its aggregate FY26 and FY27 earnings forecasts by 2.5 per cent and 5.1 per cent respectively.
The research house maintained its "Overweight" call on the technology sector and expects the momentum to continue into the second half.
It pointed to improving earnings, positive management guidance, healthy order books and high factory loadings as factors supporting the outlook.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to fuel the recovery. Heavy investment is filtering through different parts of Malaysia's semiconductor supply chain, lifting demand for wafer fabrication equipment and automated test equipment (ATE).
This is benefiting ATE and engineering support companies, while outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (Osat) players are seeing stronger earnings from higher factory loadings.
Capital expenditure linked to AI and data centre buildouts, together with demand for power-management and automotive integrated circuits, is also supporting the recovery.
RHB Research said ATE and engineering support companies are sitting on record backlogs, while Osat players are seeing record revenue and loadings.

EMS remains the weak link. The research house maintained a neutral outlook on the segment as it bottoms out, although higher seasonal demand is expected to improve utilisation and margins in the second half.
New project transfers and mass production are expected to make a more meaningful contribution by FY27.
WHO COULD BE NEXT?
As the earnings tide turns, RHB Research sees greater opportunities among technology stocks that have yet to fully catch up.
It sees more upside among laggards and second-tier stocks where improving earnings and operations have yet to be fully reflected in valuations.
The sector is trading at about 25 times forward earnings, around its five-year mean, even as earnings are projected to grow by more than 30 per cent.
In simple terms, valuations remain around historical levels despite expectations of much stronger earnings.
RHB Research's five top picks are Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI), Pentamaster Corp Bhd, CTOS Digital Bhd, Coraza Integrated Technology Bhd and JHM Consolidation Bhd.
MPI is benefiting from surging AI server-related demand, particularly for power semiconductors. It is expanding its AI server-related packaging lines to 28 from 16.
Its new Suxiang facility is expected to begin operations in the second half of its current financial year, backed by an initial business pipeline of about US$30 million.
RHB Research has a target price of RM55.80 on MPI.
Pentamaster, meanwhile, is sitting on a record RM550 million order book, supported by medical and AI-driven factory automation demand.
It is also benefiting from demand for semiconductor testing solutions used in AI and high-performance computing applications. RHB Research has a target price of RM6.32 on the company.
Among domestic-focused software and digital solutions providers, RHB Research prefers CTOS, believing most of the negatives have already been priced into the stock and earnings are poised to recover.
Its RM1.11 target price implies 73.4 per cent upside from its last closing price of 64 sen, the largest potential upside among the 12 technology stocks under RHB Research's coverage.
At the smaller end of the market, RHB Research singled out Coraza and JHM as its preferred picks, expecting both to benefit from an earnings rebound, stronger revenue and operating leverage.
Coraza is expected to deliver two consecutive years of record revenue and earnings, supported by a larger addressable market, higher-value projects, vertical integration and a broader customer base.
RHB Research has a target price of RM1.45 on Coraza.
For JHM, the research house believes the worst is behind it, with stronger recoveries expected in its semiconductor-related sheet metal and automotive businesses.
Growth is supported by new orders from existing customers, contributions from Magna Autosystems Inc and a RM300 million Proton contract secured through its JHM Dekai Auto Lighting joint venture.
RHB Research has a target price of 64 sen on JHM.

64185375fed34447: QUITO: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday designated Ecuador's Los Tiguerones gang a "terrorist organisation" during a visit to Quito, escalating Washington's campaign against criminal groups it says are destabilising Latin America.
Rubio said the gang was "linked to narcotrafficking" as well as "attacks targeting civilians, law enforcement officers, and journalists."

"We are not talking about an ordinary mafia, nor are we talking about common criminals, we are talking about terrorists who, in many cases, possess weapons and equipment resembling the national armies of certain countries," he said.
The group made international headlines in early 2024 when masked gang members stormed a TV studio during a live broadcast, firing shots and forcing terrified crew to the ground.
Once-peaceful Ecuador has been grappling with a shocking rise in cartel violence that has seen more than 25,000 people murdered in the last three years, according to official figures.
Drug gangs from Albania to Mexico have descended on the Andean nation, vying for control of routes to take drugs from South American coca fields to US, European and Asian markets.
An estimated 70 per cent of the cocaine produced in neighbouring Colombia and Peru passes through Ecuador.
Los Tiguerones have been linked to cocaine trafficking, extortion, contract killings, arms trafficking and money laundering.
It is one of Ecuador's most powerful criminal organisations, competing with Los Choneros and Los Lobos for control of prisons, ports and trafficking routes.
They are blamed for waves of violence, including the killing of rivals, prison riots, as well as kidnapping police and prison guards.
The designation freezes any US assets the group might hold and bars Americans from doing business with it.
Rubio made the announcement during a three-nation Latin America tour designed to shore up conservative allies in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and bolster US influence across the region.
Los Tiguerones is the latest Ecuadoran gang to be designated a terrorist organisation by Washington, joining Los Choneros, Los Lobos and Chone Killers.
The Trump administration has designated a number of other Latin American gangs and drug cartels as terrorist organisations, including Venezuela's Tren de Aragua and the Mexican Sinaloa cartel.
67615c28195718d9: QUITO: US secretary of state Marco Rubio visited Ecuador Wednesday to press the fight against "narco-terrorists" who have transformed the country into one of Latin America's most violent.
Rubio visited Quito as the second stop on a three-nation tour designed to shore up conservative allies in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and bolster US influence across the region.

In Colombia on Tuesday, Rubio pledged to restore "natural relations" with Bogota after years of leftist rule.
